issues.legal_issue: A temporary secondary commercial activity carried on alongside the business for which premises were leased does not amount to an actionable change of user when it does not prejudice the landlord’s interest.
material_facts: The premises were leased for a cycle and rickshaw repair business.
The tenant continued the repair business while also selling televisions for about seven months, then stopped selling them because the business was not viable.
The lease did not expressly prohibit the tenant from conducting any business other than cycle or rickshaw repairs.
The tenant had not obtained the landlord’s consent to start selling televisions.
The landlord sought eviction on the ground that the premises had been put to a different use; the eviction order was challenged by the tenant.
issues.conclusion: The temporary sale of televisions alongside the continuing repair business did not constitute a change of user that entitled the landlord to eviction. The appeal was allowed, and the eviction order was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(2)(ii)(b) of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, restricts a tenant’s use of leased premises to protect the landlord’s interests. It is akin to Section 108(o) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, which prohibits use for a purpose other than that for which the property was leased. The concept of injury to the premises underlying Section 108(o) informs the statutory eviction ground: ordinarily, a small change in use is not actionable if the landlord’s interest is not prejudiced. Applying Mohan Lal v. Jai Bhagwan, the Court held that the temporary additional business here did not amount to a change of user; Des Raj v. Sham Lal, concerning premises used exclusively as a godown rather than as a shop, did not govern the case. The Court also referred to U Po Naing v. Burma Oil Co. and decisions of the Kerala and Bombay High Courts concerning whether a different trade injures the leased property.

rule.if: tenant_appeal_challenges_eviction_for_change_of_use and premises_leased_for_commercial_repair and original_repair_business_continued and secondary_business_was_temporary and landlord_interest_was_not_prejudiced

predicates.tenant_appeal_challenges_eviction_for_ch: The tenant appealed an eviction order founded on an alleged change in the use of the premises.
predicates.premises_leased_for_commercial_repair: The premises were leased for a commercial repair business.
predicates.original_repair_business_continued: The tenant continued the repair business for which the premises were leased.
predicates.secondary_business_was_temporary: The tenant carried on an additional business only temporarily alongside the original business.
predicates.landlord_interest_was_not_prejudiced: The additional business did not prejudice the landlord’s interest in the leased premises.
predicates.eviction_not_warranted_for_change_of_use: Eviction is not warranted on the ground of change of user.

issues.definition: When a tenant appeals an eviction order based on change of use, and the premises were leased for commercial repair, the original business continued, the additional business was temporary, and the landlord’s interest was not prejudiced, eviction is not warranted for change of user.
